verses.text: About Moab. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "How terrible for Nebo, because it will be destroyed! Kiriathaim will be put to shame and captured. The fortress will be put to shame and torn down.
No one will praise Moab anymore. In Heshbon people plot her downfall: 'Come, let us put an end to her as a nation.' You too, town of Madmen, will be silenced. The sword will chase you.
Listen to the cries from Horonaim: ruin and great destruction!
Moab is crushed. Her little ones cry out.
People climb the road up to Luhith, weeping bitterly as they go. On the road down to Horonaim they hear cries of anguish over the destruction.
Run! Save your lives! Be like a bush in the desert.
Because you trusted in what you made and in your riches, you too will be captured. Your god Chemosh will go into exile, along with his priests and officials.
The destroyer will come against every town, and not one town will escape. The valley will be ruined and the plain destroyed, as the LORD has said.
Give wings to Moab so she can fly away, because her towns will become ruins with no one living in them.
A curse on anyone who is lazy in doing the LORD's work! A curse on anyone who holds back their sword from bloodshed!

Moab has been at ease since its youth, like wine left to settle on its dregs. It has never been poured from one jar to another. It has never gone into exile. So its flavor has stayed the same, and its smell has not changed.
But look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will send people to pour it out. They will empty its jars and smash them to pieces.
Then Moab will be ashamed of its god Chemosh, just as the people of Israel were ashamed when they trusted in Bethel.
How can you say, 'We are warriors, strong men ready for battle'?
Moab will be destroyed, and its towns invaded. Its finest young men will go down to be slaughtered," says the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.
"Moab's disaster is close at hand. Its downfall is coming quickly.
Mourn for Moab, all you who live around it, all who know its fame. Say, 'How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff!'
Come down from your place of honor and sit on the dry ground, you people living in Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come against you and torn down your fortresses.
You who live in Aroer, stand by the road and watch. Ask those who are running away, the man fleeing and the woman escaping, 'What has happened?'
Moab is put to shame, because it is shattered. Wail and cry out! Announce by the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.
Judgment has come on the plateau: on Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
on Dibon, Nebo, and Beth Diblathaim,
on Kiriathaim, Beth Gamul, and Beth Meon,
on Kerioth and Bozrah, and on all the towns of Moab, far and near.
Moab's strength is cut off. Its arm is broken," says the LORD.
"Make Moab drunk, because it has been arrogant toward the LORD. Let Moab roll around in its vomit and become a joke.
Didn't you make fun of Israel? Was Israel caught among thieves, that you shake your head in scorn every time you speak of them?
Leave your towns and live among the rocks, you people of Moab. Be like a dove that makes its nest at the mouth of a cave.
We have heard about Moab's pride. It is very proud, so high and mighty, so arrogant and full of itself.
I know how insolent it is," says the LORD, "but it means nothing. Its boasting accomplishes nothing.
So I will wail for Moab. I will cry out for all of Moab. I will mourn for the people of Kir Hareseth.

I will weep for you, vines of Sibmah, even more than the people of Jazer weep. Your branches reached as far as the sea. They reached the sea of Jazer. But the destroyer has attacked your summer fruit and your grape harvest.
Joy and gladness are gone from the fruitful fields of Moab. I have stopped the flow of wine from the winepresses. No one stomps the grapes with shouts of joy. There are shouts, but not shouts of joy.
Their cries can be heard from Heshbon to Elealeh and Jahaz, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath Shelishiyah. Even the waters of Nimrim have dried up.
In Moab I will put an end," says the LORD, "to those who make offerings at the high places and burn incense to their gods.
So my heart moans for Moab like the sad music of a flute. My heart moans like a flute for the people of Kir Hareseth. The wealth they gained is gone.
Every head is shaved and every beard cut off. Every hand is gashed, and every waist is wrapped in sackcloth.
On all the roofs of Moab and in its streets there is nothing but mourning, because I have smashed Moab like a jar no one wants," says the LORD.
"How shattered it is! How they wail! How Moab turns its back in shame! Moab has become a joke and a horror to all its neighbors."
For this is what the LORD says: "Look, an enemy swoops down like an eagle, spreading its wings over Moab.
Kerioth will be captured, and its fortresses taken. On that day the hearts of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Moab will be destroyed as a nation, because it was arrogant toward the LORD.
Terror, pits, and traps are waiting for you, people of Moab," says the LORD.
"Whoever runs from the terror will fall into a pit. Whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in a trap. For I will bring on Moab the year of its punishment," says the LORD.

"In the shadow of Heshbon, those running away stand without strength. For a fire has gone out from Heshbon, a flame from the house of Sihon. It burns the foreheads of Moab, the skulls of those noisy boasters.
How terrible for you, Moab! The people of Chemosh are destroyed. Your sons are taken into exile, and your daughters into captivity.
But in the days to come I will bring Moab back from captivity," says the LORD. This is the end of the judgment on Moab.
